chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim and Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever makes a bequest of one-third has harmed the heirs, and a bequest of one-fifth and one-quarter is superior to a bequest of one-third.

Second: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb ibn Ya'qub, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who dies, what is his share of his wealth? He said to him: One-third of his wealth, and the wife also [receives her share].

Third: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: That I make a bequest of one-fifth of my wealth is more beloved to me than that I make a bequest of one-quarter, and that I make a bequest of one-quarter is more beloved to me than that I make a bequest of one-third.

And whoever makes a bequest of one-third and does not leave [enough for heirs], having reached the limit, and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man who died and bequeathed all his wealth or most of it, he said: The bequest is returned from the excessive part to the rightful heirs.
Whoever wrongs himself and includes in his bequest the excessive and unjust portion, then it is returned from the excessive part, and the heirs are left with their inheritance.

And he said: Whoever bequeaths one-third of his wealth and does not leave [enough], having reached the limit, then he said: That I bequeath one-fifth of my wealth is more beloved to me than that I bequeath one-quarter.
ai.seo_question: What is the best amount to bequeath in a will according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration, rooted in the teachings of the Imams, establishes a hierarchy for bequests where one-fifth is preferred over one-quarter, and one-quarter over one-third, to prevent impoverishing the heirs. It highlights the principle of 'returning the known from the unknown' (al-wasiyyah turadd ila al-ma'ruf), ensuring that excessive bequests do not unjustly deprive heirs of their Quranic shares, a concept reinforced by Imam al-Sadiq and attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin.
